scenarios.scenario_description: A student is presented with a cell containing aqueous copper(II) sulfate and inert carbon electrodes. They must predict the products. Another student uses copper electrodes instead.
scenarios.key_insight: Inert electrodes force water oxidation at the anode ($O_2$ produced), while active copper electrodes result in the anode dissolving ($Cu ightarrow Cu^{2+} + 2e^-$) to maintain concentration.
discrimination_factors: Recall of anode half-equation for aqueous sulfates

scenarios.scenario_description: Equal masses of products are collected at the cathode in two separate beakers: one contains molten KCl, the other aqueous $CuSO_4$. The student is asked to compare the volume of gas produced at the anodes (or the charge required).
scenarios.key_insight: For Potassium (Group 1), 1 mole of electrons produces 1 mole of K (39g). For Copper (Transition metal), 2 moles of electrons produce 1 mole of Cu (63.5g). Producing equal masses requires vastly different amounts of charge and results in different gas volumes ($Cl_2$ vs $O_2$).

scenarios.scenario_description: Concentrated aqueous NaCl is electrolysed. The solution is tested with Universal Indicator or a pH probe after the reaction stops.
scenarios.key_insight: Discharging $Cl^-$ prevents $OH^-$ from being discharged at the anode, while $H^+$ is discharged at the cathode. Removal of $H^+$ leaves an excess of $OH^-$, resulting in an alkaline solution (pH > 7).
discrimination_factors: Discharge preference of halides vs hydroxide in concentrated solutions

scenarios.scenario_description: A student electrolyses molten $Al_2O_3$ and is given a rate of electron flow in 'moles of electrons per second'. They must calculate the mass of Aluminum produced in a specific duration (e.g., 48 seconds).
scenarios.key_insight: The calculation requires linking the rate ($mol \cdot s^{-1}$) to total moles of electrons, then applying the mole ratio for the reduction half-equation ($Al^{3+} + 3e^- ightarrow Al$).
discrimination_factors: Avoiding errors with isotope masses or unit conversions
